res.reason: The claim misattributes the statement: the 200-test figure appears in Fortune's 2015 Theranos coverage and a Theranos letter describing Theranos's own offerings, not in any current fortune.com offering.

claim: Holmes will only say–and this is more than she has ever said before–that her company uses “the same fundamental chemical methods” as existing labs do.

res.reason: Prosecutors and reporting on the Holmes trial (NPR, ABC News, WJTV) establish that Theranos secretly used conventional, traditional blood-testing machines and methods, having modified them, rather than its own novel chemistry.

page: B1 "never used commercially available lab equipment"

res.reason: Nothing found confirms this, and no source says the opposite.
res.reason_as_of: The retrieved evidence concerns Theranos's use of its own finger-prick technology, not whether Business Insider as a publication has used lab equipment for finger-stick tests; the claim appears to be a category error about the wrong entity, so none of the sources bear on it.
